skills.title: Big letters A–Z
skills.objective: Recognise uppercase letters A to Z.
skills.explanation: Uppercase letters are the big forms we often see at the start of names and signs.

workedExample.headline: Meet a big letter
workedExample.caption: This is uppercase A. A can begin Apple.

skills.title: Small letters a–z
skills.objective: Recognise lowercase letters a to z.
skills.explanation: Lowercase letters are the smaller forms used in most words.

workedExample.headline: Meet a small letter
workedExample.caption: This is lowercase a. It is the small partner of A.

skills.title: Big and small partners
skills.objective: Match uppercase letters with their lowercase partners.
skills.explanation: Every alphabet letter has a big uppercase form and a small lowercase form.

workedExample.headline: Partners belong together
workedExample.caption: A and a are two forms of the same letter.

skills.title: Letter, word and picture
skills.objective: Connect a letter with a familiar word and picture.
skills.explanation: A letter can start a familiar word. The picture helps us remember the word and its first letter.

workedExample.headline: A for Apple
workedExample.caption: A is for Apple. Apple begins with A.

skills.title: Letter sounds
skills.objective: Connect familiar letters with clear, simple sound examples.
skills.explanation: Listen to the first sound in a familiar word and connect it to the letter used in that example. BrightQuest keeps irregular vowel sounds, Q, X, and consonant clusters out of simple Nursery sound mastery.

workedExample.headline: Listen to Mango
workedExample.caption: Mango starts with a clear beginning sound linked to M.

skills.title: Listen and find the letter
skills.objective: Listen to a letter name or cue and select it.
skills.explanation: Good listening helps us find a letter even when we are not copying a shape.

workedExample.headline: Listen, then choose
workedExample.caption: If you hear “D”, look carefully before tapping.

skills.title: Beginning sounds
skills.objective: Match a familiar word to its clear beginning letter-sound example.
skills.explanation: The first sound we hear can help us connect a familiar word to its starting letter. Simple Nursery practice avoids irregular or advanced sound patterns.

workedExample.headline: Listen to Ball
workedExample.caption: Ball begins with the clear beginning sound linked to B.

skills.title: Look closely at letters
skills.objective: Notice small visual differences between letters.
skills.explanation: Some letters look similar. We can slow down and notice stems, curves and direction.

workedExample.headline: b is not d
workedExample.caption: The round part is on a different side.

skills.title: Trace big letters
skills.objective: Practise following a broad uppercase letter path with touch or mouse.
skills.explanation: Tracing here is motor practice only. BrightQuest checks broad ordered guide points, not handwriting quality.

workedExample.headline: Follow the A path
workedExample.caption: Start at the dot and move through the guide points in order.

skills.title: Trace small letters
skills.objective: Practise following a broad lowercase letter path with touch or mouse.
skills.explanation: Tracing here checks only whether broad guide checkpoints are followed in order; it does not score handwriting correctness.

workedExample.headline: Follow the a path
workedExample.caption: Move through the guide points gently and in order.

skills.title: Numbers 0–5
skills.objective: Recognise numerals from 0 to 5.
skills.explanation: A numeral is a written mark that tells us a number. We begin with 0 to 5.

workedExample.headline: Meet 3
workedExample.caption: The numeral 3 can represent three objects.

skills.title: Numbers 6–10
skills.objective: Recognise numerals from 6 to 10.
skills.explanation: After 5 come 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.

workedExample.headline: Meet 8
workedExample.caption: Eight means a group of eight.

skills.title: Numbers 11–20
skills.objective: Recognise numerals from 11 to 20.
skills.explanation: Teen numbers have two digits. We look at both digits carefully.

workedExample.headline: Meet 14
workedExample.caption: Fourteen is ten and four more.

skills.title: Count 0–5 objects
skills.objective: Count visible objects up to five.
skills.explanation: Touch or point to each object once while counting. If there are none, the count is zero.

workedExample.headline: Count the apples
workedExample.caption: One, two, three apples.

skills.title: Count 6–10 objects
skills.objective: Count visible groups from six to ten.
skills.explanation: For a bigger group, move your eyes from left to right and count each object once.

workedExample.headline: Count in a row
workedExample.caption: There are six stars.

skills.title: Number and quantity partners
skills.objective: Match a numeral to a group with that many objects.
skills.explanation: The numeral and the group should tell the same amount.

workedExample.headline: 3 matches three dots
workedExample.caption: The number 3 and three dots are partners.

skills.title: Missing numbers
skills.objective: Find the missing numeral in a simple counting sequence.
skills.explanation: Numbers have an order. Count forward and notice which number is missing.

workedExample.caption: Three belongs between 2 and 4.

skills.title: More and less
skills.objective: Compare two visible groups to find which has more or less.
skills.explanation: More means a bigger amount. Less means a smaller amount. We can count if we are unsure.

workedExample.headline: Which has more?
workedExample.caption: Three dots are more than two dots.

skills.title: Same and different
skills.objective: Notice whether two amounts or objects are the same or different.
skills.explanation: Same means they match in the way we are checking. Different means something does not match.

workedExample.headline: Same amount
workedExample.caption: Both groups have three objects.

skills.title: Add with objects
skills.objective: Combine two small groups and count the total, up to 10.
skills.explanation: Addition joins groups. First see each group, then bring them together and count all objects once.

workedExample.headline: 1 apple + 1 apple
workedExample.caption: One and one more makes two.

skills.title: Very easy number addition
skills.objective: Use numerals after understanding groups, with totals no more than 10.
skills.explanation: The plus sign tells us to combine amounts. We can still imagine or draw objects to help.

workedExample.caption: Two plus one equals three.

skills.title: Colours
skills.objective: Recognise and name familiar colours.
skills.explanation: Colours help us describe what we see.

workedExample.headline: Find red
workedExample.caption: A red circle is red.

skills.title: 2D shapes
skills.objective: Recognise circle, square, triangle and rectangle.
skills.explanation: A shape can be noticed by its sides and corners.

workedExample.headline: Meet a triangle
workedExample.caption: A triangle has three straight sides.

skills.title: Animals
skills.objective: Recognise and name familiar animals.
skills.explanation: We can notice animals by their body, sound and where we commonly see them.

workedExample.headline: Meet a dog
workedExample.caption: This familiar animal is a dog.

skills.title: Fruits and vegetables
skills.objective: Recognise familiar fruits and vegetables without judging food choices.
skills.explanation: Fruits and vegetables come in many colours, shapes and tastes.

workedExample.headline: Apple and carrot
workedExample.caption: Apple is a fruit; carrot is a vegetable in this activity.

skills.title: Familiar objects
skills.objective: Recognise familiar everyday objects and simple uses.
skills.explanation: Objects around us have names and uses.

workedExample.headline: A cup is for drinking
workedExample.caption: We can use a cup for drinking.

skills.title: Body parts
skills.objective: Name familiar external body parts safely.
skills.explanation: We use simple names for visible body parts in everyday learning.

workedExample.headline: Eyes help us see
workedExample.caption: These are eyes.

skills.title: Everyday routines
skills.objective: Put simple everyday actions in sensible order.
skills.explanation: Some routines have a helpful order, like washing hands before eating.

workedExample.headline: Wash, then eat
workedExample.caption: We wash hands before eating.

skills.title: Simple patterns
skills.objective: Continue a simple repeating visual pattern.
skills.explanation: A repeating pattern follows the same small rule again and again.

workedExample.headline: Red, blue, red, blue
workedExample.caption: The next colour would be red.

skills.title: Match same things
skills.objective: Match pictures or symbols that belong as identical partners.
skills.explanation: Matching means looking for another item that is the same in the way we are checking.

workedExample.headline: Find the same
workedExample.caption: The two apples match.

skills.title: Sort into groups
skills.objective: Put items into simple named groups using a clear rule.
skills.explanation: Sorting means grouping things that share a feature.

workedExample.headline: Fruit or animal?
workedExample.caption: Apple goes with fruit; dog goes with animal.

skills.title: Look, remember and listen
skills.objective: Use short visual memory, observation and listening clues.
skills.explanation: We can look carefully, remember one small detail and listen for a simple instruction.

workedExample.headline: Remember: star, ball
workedExample.caption: After a short look, we can recall what we saw.
